method: Six actual functions.view_image opens in source/candidate pairs. Each source was read before its corresponding candidate. No crops, reopens, new screenshots, or full source inventory.

figures.originalScopedComparison: The original places X below the nearer rightward arrow tip and X1 below the farther tip on the common horizontal baseline. The filled AB rod lies above that baseline, to the right of O1 and before both tips. This is the affected relationship attribution, not a rebuilt source inventory.
figures.candidateScopedObservation: At the existing 640px neutral screenshot, X remains directly below the nearer tip and X1 below the farther tip. Both glyphs are below the shaft with visible white clearance, are separated from each other, and are not clipped at the right edge. The additional 2px downward placement does not redirect either label toward A/B, the rod, or the clock annotations.

changedLabelApproval.judgment: The two labels identify their own axis tips, not a rod endpoint or timing annotation. The observed separation is usable and unambiguous, not merely a native collision-report pass.

figures.unchangedContent: Clock and same-t additions are visible but their physics, source relationship fidelity, and language approvals are inherited from D1226, not newly reviewed.

figures.originalScopedComparison: The original locates A below the rod's left endpoint, to the right of O1; B is below its right endpoint. The l0 dimension occupies a separate lower row. X1 labels the far right axis tip. These endpoint/dimension distinctions define the affected attribution.
figures.candidateScopedObservation: A is still southwest of the rod's left endpoint and below the baseline. Moving it 6px right makes a distinct space after O1 without moving it beyond the endpoint or onto its vertical guide. The endpoint's guide descends farther right, while the l0 text is centered in a separate lower dimension row. X1 sits below its own rightward tip with white clearance and remains within the image.

changedLabelApproval.judgment: O1 and A read as separate labels. A is attributable to the left rod endpoint, not the origin or a dimension; the X1 shift retains axis-tip identity. No stroke crosses either changed glyph.

figures.unchangedContent: The rod, B endpoint, opposing optical arrows, and length dimension are unchanged. Their semantic approval is inherited rather than replayed.

figures.originalScopedComparison: In the original, A and B flank the filled first rod above the common horizontal baseline. O1 is below and left of A. The upper l+v tau1 dimension and the intervening v tau1 shift are separately labelled; the lower A1B1 and A2B2 rod states have their own endpoint labels. X/X1 are below the two rightward tips.
figures.candidateScopedObservation: A and B now sit at the height of the filled first rod's upper edge, on its west/east sides. They are adjacent to that first rod, not the outlined later rods. Both are visibly above the horizontal shafts; neither axis runs through a glyph. A is vertically separated from O1. The upper dimension line and l+v tau1 text are farther above, while v tau1 is below the first row, so neither endpoint label can reasonably be read as a dimension label. X/X1 remain below their respective tips and visibly distinct.

changedLabelApproval.judgment: The repaired A/B pair clearly identifies the first rod's endpoints and resolves the observed axis strikes and A/O1 crowding. W/E attribution is retained. The two axis-tip labels remain correctly attributed and readable. This is an actual visual clearance judgment on the candidate screenshot.

figures.unchangedContent: Successive-position geometry, dimensions, event-time labels, and one-way c cues reuse D1226's independent semantic PASS only. No full optical or physics review was repeated.
